what_its_for: This medicine is used to manage heavy menstrual bleeding caused by uterine fibroids (noncancerous growths in the uterus) in women who have not yet gone through menopause. Elagolix reduces the hormones that cause fibroids to grow, while estradiol and norethindrone are added to help prevent bone loss and reduce other side effects caused by lower hormone levels.
how_to_take: Take this medicine by mouth exactly as your doctor tells you. You will take TWO different capsules each day: one yellow-and-white capsule in the MORNING (contains elagolix, estradiol, and norethindrone) and one yellow capsule in the EVENING (contains only elagolix). Swallow the capsules whole with or without food. Try to take them at the same times every day to help you remember. Do not crush, chew, or open the capsules.
dosing: The usual dose is: ONE yellow-and-white capsule (150 mg elagolix / 1 mg estradiol / 0.5 mg norethindrone acetate) taken every morning, AND ONE yellow capsule (300 mg elagolix) taken every evening. Treatment should last no longer than 24 months total because this medicine can cause bone loss with long-term use. Your doctor will prescribe the lowest effective dose for the shortest time needed.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember on the same day. If it is already the next day, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular schedule. Do NOT take two doses on the same day to make up for a missed one. If you are unsure what to do, call your pharmacist or doctor.
storage: Store at room temperature between 68°F and 77°F (20°C to 25°C). Keep the capsules in their original packaging and away from moisture and heat. Do NOT store in the bathroom. Keep this medicine out of reach of children and pets. Dispose of any unused medicine safely — ask your pharmacist about a drug take-back program.
what_to_avoid: Do NOT take this medicine if you are pregnant or think you may be pregnant — it can harm an unborn baby. Use a non-hormonal form of birth control (such as condoms) since this medicine is NOT a contraceptive. Avoid taking certain medicines without checking with your doctor first, including: other hormonal products, certain seizure medicines (like carbamazepine, phenytoin), rifampin, St. John's Wort, and some antifungals or HIV medicines — these can affect how Oriahnn works. Limit alcohol use, as alcohol combined with estrogen may increase breast cancer risk. Avoid smoking, as it increases the risk of serious heart and blood vessel problems when taking hormone-containing medicines.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or go to the emergency room if you experience: sudden chest pain, shortness of breath, or coughing up blood (possible blood clot in the lungs); pain, swelling, or redness in your leg (possible blood clot); sudden severe headache, vision changes, weakness, or difficulty speaking (possible stroke); yellowing of the skin or eyes (liver problems); unusual vaginal bleeding or discharge; signs of an allergic reaction such as rash, hives, swelling of the face, lips, or throat, or difficulty breathing; symptoms of depression, mood changes, or thoughts of self-harm; or bone pain or fractures. Also tell your doctor if you develop any new breast lumps or have significant bone density concerns.
when_it_works: You may start to notice lighter periods or reduced bleeding within the first 1 to 2 menstrual cycles (about 1 to 2 months) of starting treatment. Many women see significant improvement by the third month. Continue taking the medicine as prescribed even if you feel better. Talk to your doctor about how long you should stay on treatment, as it is limited to 24 months.
special_populations: PREGNANCY: Do NOT use this medicine during pregnancy. If you become pregnant while taking it, stop immediately and contact your doctor. Use non-hormonal contraception during treatment. BREASTFEEDING: This medicine may pass into breast milk and could harm a nursing baby. Talk to your doctor before breastfeeding. LIVER PROBLEMS: Do not use this medicine if you have known liver problems or liver disease. BONE HEALTH: This medicine can reduce bone density, especially with longer use. Your doctor may monitor your bone health. Women with osteoporosis or risk factors for bone loss should discuss the risks carefully with their doctor. HEART AND BLOOD VESSEL DISEASE: Women with a history of heart attack, stroke, blood clots, or certain heart conditions should not use this medicine. HORMONE-SENSITIVE CONDITIONS: Women with a history of certain cancers (such as breast or uterine cancer) or other hormone-sensitive conditions should not use this medicine. Always tell your doctor about all your medical conditions and all medicines, vitamins, and supplements you take.
